title: Welcome to My Blog
text:
Hello! Welcome to my personal blog. This is where I’ll be sharing my thoughts, learnings, and insights about:

Machine Learning & AI: Latest developments, techniques, and applications
Engineering: Problem-solving approaches and technical solutions
Career & Growth: Lessons learned and experiences in tech
Life & Learning: Personal reflections and continuous learning journey

I believe in keeping things simple and focused. This blog is my digital notebook where I capture ideas, document learning, and share what I discover along the way.


I’ll be writing about:

Technical deep-dives into ML/AI topics
Career insights and lessons learned
Tools and techniques I find useful
Thoughts on the future of technology




Feel free to reach out to me on Twitter or LinkedIn if you’d like to discuss any of these topics!
Happy reading! 🚀

title: Ayush Thakur
text:
I build and evaluate AI systems.
I am a Manager, AI Engineering at Weights & Biases by CoreWeave. I am currently working on internal coding agents, evaluation harnesses, memory, and systems that improve through their own experience.
Previously, I was a growth MLE at W&B. I built open-source MLOps and LLMOps integrations, production RAG systems such as Wandbot, technical courses, and a large body of practical ML writing. My work helped grow W&B’s brand and made its tools more useful and accessible to the ML community.
I began working on autonomous robots and computer vision early in my career, and that experience shaped how I approach engineering: move with urgency, stay close to real problems, learn by building, and take ownership from an idea through to a working outcome. I am always interested in collaborating with researchers and engineers who want to turn ambitious questions into useful systems and share what we learn along the way.

title: About
text:
How I work
I am drawn to the part of AI engineering that is difficult to see in a demo: instrumentation, datasets, failure analysis, evaluation criteria, and the feedback loops that make a system improve. I enjoy moving between implementation and explanation—building a tool, stress-testing it, and then writing or teaching the reusable idea behind it.
That pattern connects most of my work: integrations that expose what a model is doing, evaluations that replace intuition with evidence, and courses that turn months of engineering lessons into a path someone else can follow.

title: About
text:
The “Enginear” story
When I was ten, a teacher asked what I wanted to become. I said “engineer.” Asked to spell it, I got it wrong, and was told that someone who could not spell the word could not become one.
I kept the misspelling—Enginear—as a reminder that an early mistake is not a verdict. Curiosity, practice, and the willingness to keep building matter much more.
